newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLO market eyes French franc, OAT spread.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLO market eyes French franc, OAT spread.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended higher with Bunds on Tuesday and are seen rangebound in coming days as investor interest is minimal and no major U.S. data are due.
Dealers said the market was lacklustre, but added they were keeping a close eye on the French franc and the OAT/Bund spread, following president Chirac's snap election call.
"If there is any pressure on the French franc or the OAT/Bund spread, our OLO/Bund spread could widen to 15 even 20 basis points," one dealer said.
The 2007 OLO yield ended at 5.99 percent, from 6.00 Monday, 14 bps over Bunds (13).
The Belgian franc ended slightly weaker at 20.6310/25 (20.6320/30), above its 20.6255 central rate to the mark.
Short-term money yields remained well above the 3.00 percent official central rate, as is always the case when the franc weakens a bit.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
